speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your infant's condition, could you please describe exactly when these episodes of stridor and wheezing occur? Specifically, do they happen during feeding, crying, or only when the baby is calm?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does extending the infant's neck or placing him in a prone position relieve the stridor and wheezing symptoms? I would also like to see if there are any visible neck masses or asymmetry. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant exhibit a cough that sounds like a "barking" seal, and have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or drooling? REQUEST TEST: Lateral Neck X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the position-dependent nature of the stridor that improves with neck extension, I suspect a vascular compression rather than an airway structural abnormality. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the Neck
